adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs outside any try/catch after the `prisma.booking.update` attendee `createMany` has already committed (line 92), so a throw from the calendar integration returns a raw 500 while the guests stay persisted, and the user's retry then fails with `BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests now count as existing attendees, leaving the calendar permanently unsynced and no emails sent (anchor 75, P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guests are persisted first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is called with no surrounding try/catch or compensating rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error after the DB commit, leaving the new attendees saved but the calendar update and subsequent `sendAddGuestsEmails` (which comes later) not executed. On a retry, `uniqueGuests` filters out already-added attendee emails and can hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` causing `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), matching the reported stuck/unsynced state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no uniqueness refine on the server (only the client checks for duplicates), so one request can insert any number of attendee rows (including repeats of the same email via `createMany`) and trigger one outbound email per row plus a calendar attendee update carrying all of them (anchor 100, P2)

adjudication.rationale: The server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates email format (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) and does not enforce a maximum length or uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but does not de-duplicate within the `guests` array itself, so duplicates in a single request can flow into `guestsFullDetails` and be passed to `attendees.createMany`. The mutation also calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original (potentially duplicated/unbounded) `guests` list, which can amplify outbound email sending and calendar attendee updates. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness/abuse issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — `guest === attendee.email` compares case-sensitively while the blacklist is lowercased, so `Bob@x.com` against an existing `bob@x.com` is treated as new, which creates a duplicate attendee row and sends a second invitation and calendar attendee to the same inbox (anchor 75, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Both checks are case-sensitive because `guest` is not normalized (e.g., `toLowerCase()`), while the blacklist is explicitly lowercased. This allows `Bob@x.com` to bypass an existing attendee `bob@x.com` and the blacklist, leading to duplicate attendee creation via `attendees.createMany` and potentially duplicate downstream effects (calendar update/emails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — attendee authorization is a case-sensitive `attendee.email === user.email` match that also accepts every attendee of a seated booking, so any seat holder can inject guests into a shared booking and cause invites containing the full attendee list (evt.attendees at :123, replyTo at organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25) to be sent to newly added arbitrary addresses, exposing other seat holders' emails even when seatsShowAttendees is false (anchor 50, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the subsequent `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`). That email comparison is case-sensitive, and more importantly it permits any attendee of a booking (including a “seated”/multi-attendee booking, as suggested by `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` being carried into `evt`) to add arbitrary guest emails. The handler then builds `evt.attendees` from *all* booking attendees (no filtering based on `seatsShowAttendees`) and `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` sets `replyTo` to `[organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, which will expose all attendee emails to recipients/newly added addresses regardless of `seatsShowAttendees` intent. This is a real privacy/security issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — the booking lookup is not filtered by status or end time, so an authorized user can add guests to CANCELLED/REJECTED or past bookings and send "CONFIRMED" METHOD:REQUEST invites for meetings that do not exist, a ready-made phishing vector under the organizer's name (anchor 75, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` with no constraints on booking state (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED) or time (e.g., `endTime < now`). The handler then updates attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), updates calendar attendees, and sends emails/ICS via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (see `packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts`), meaning this can send fresh confirmed invites even for cancelled/rejected or past bookings. That is a real, diff-grounded correctness/security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` uses AND instead of OR and no org-admin check exists, so team admins and org admins are denied (fail-closed, but the authorization matrix is wrong and the resulting workaround pressure is toward loosening it); separately, team hosts of round-robin/collective bookings who are not `booking.userId` are not covered (anchor 75, P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the authorization flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the caller to be both team admin and team owner to pass the `isTeamAdminOrOwner` check. Given the variable name and typical role semantics, this is very likely incorrect (should be OR), causing legitimate team admins (but not owners) to be denied. The handler otherwise only permits `booking.userId === user.id` (organizer) or an existing attendee email match, so any other team role (including non-`booking.userId` hosts) is excluded by this diff’s logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is built from the caller's (`ctx.user`) credentials rather than the booking owner's, so when an attendee or team admin invokes the mutation, `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs the organizer's booking references against the caller's connected calendar accounts, operating on third-party calendar data with the wrong principal instead of updating the organizer's event (anchor 50, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly permits non-organizers (`isAttendee` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`) to call it, but then constructs `EventManager` using the caller (`ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (near the end: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`). This means calendar updates will be attempted using the invoker’s connected calendar accounts rather than the booking owner/organizer’s credentials, which can lead to incorrect updates/failures and is a verifiable principal mismatch introduced by this diff.
